items.t: Proposed space tourism as a way to boost Nevada's entertainment business.
items.q: Nevada Lt. Gov. Stavros Anthony has an unusual plan to rev up the Silver State's entertainment business: space tourism.

record.t: Has served alongside Gov. Joe Lombardo in leading Nevada since 2022.
record.q: He ran a spirited campaign for mayor of Las Vegas and, since 2022, has served alongside Gov. Joe Lombardo , leading the Silver State.

record.t: Ran on the Lombardo/Anthony ticket, which defeated an incumbent Democratic governor and lieutenant governor.
record.q: The Lombardo/Anthony ticket was the only one in America in which Republicans defeated an incumbent Democratic governor and lieutenant governor.

record.t: Began a career with the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department in 1980 and later served as a captain overseeing its Financial and Property Crimes Bureau.
record.q: Anthony began his career with Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department in 1980 and most recently served the community as a captain overseeing the Financial and Property Crimes Bureau of the department.

record.office: Nevada System of Higher Education Board of Regents
record.t: Served as a regent in the state's higher education system.
record.q: He had a nearly three-decade career in law enforcement, was a regent in the state's higher education system and served as a longtime Las Vegas city councilman.

record.t: Served as a City of Las Vegas Councilman.
record.q: a member of the Nevada System of Higher Education Board of Regents, as a City of Las Vegas Councilman and now as Nevada Lieutenant Governor.
As Nevada's 37th Lieutenant Governor, Stavros Anthony serves Nevadans in a variety of ways.

record.t: Was fined by the Nevada Commission on Ethics for using state resources to promote his task force on transgender-identifying athletes.
record.q: The Nevada Commission on Ethics on Wednesday fined Lt. Gov. Stavros Anthony for using state resources to promote his task force on transgender-identifying athletes.

record.t: Was found by the Nevada Commission on Ethics, in a 3-2 vote, to have violated state ethics laws, and was assessed a $3,000 civil penalty and required to complete ethics training.
record.q: In a 3-2 vote, the commission determined Anthony violated state ethics laws. As part of their formal rebuke, members imposed a $3,000 civil penalty and mandated completion of ethics training.
